title: Statistical and Model Visualizations
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of statistical and model visualizations and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply distribution comparisons in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Statistical and Model Visualizations is part of Data Visualization and Graphics. Start with distribution comparisons and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: A useful visualization encodes the question honestly with readable scales, descriptive labels and a clear account of uncertainty or limits.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: A useful visualization encodes the question honestly with readable scales, descriptive labels and a clear account of uncertainty or limits. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Distribution Comparisons
items.text: For distribution comparisons, state the statistical question and assumptions first, then describe the estimate or diagnostic in context.

items.title: Regression Lines and Confidence Bands
items.text: For regression lines and confidence bands, state the statistical question and assumptions first, then describe the estimate or diagnostic in context.

items.title: Residual Plots
items.text: For residual plots, label the variables and units, check the visual scale, and state what the graphic cannot prove.

items.title: Diagnostic Charts
items.text: Turn diagnostic charts into a check with a clear condition, expected result and an example that should fail.

items.title: Model Performance Visualization
items.text: For model performance visualization, state the statistical question and assumptions first, then describe the estimate or diagnostic in context.

items.title: Uncertainty Visualization
items.text: For uncertainty visualization, label the variables and units, check the visual scale, and state what the graphic cannot prove.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Choose a chart for the variables, label axes and units, and state what the plot cannot establish. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Statistical and Model Visualizations
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 125: Statistical and Model Visualizations
plot(c(8, 9, 10), c(2, 5, 4), type = "b", xlab = "Observation", ylab = "Measure")
content_blocks.expected_output: A labelled plot window shows three synthetic observations joined by lines.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For statistical and model visualizations, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a p-value, coefficient or score as a complete conclusion.
common_mistakes.why: Study design, assumptions, effect size and uncertainty shape interpretation.
common_mistakes.fix: State the question, inspect diagnostics and report uncertainty and limitations.

common_mistakes.problem: Using test data during feature selection or tuning.
common_mistakes.why: This leaks information and leads to an overly optimistic evaluation.
common_mistakes.fix: Separate training, validation and final test roles before modeling.

common_mistakes.problem: Reporting a model without comparing it with a baseline.
common_mistakes.why: Complexity does not guarantee useful performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Evaluate an appropriate simple baseline with task-relevant metrics.
